elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: "and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf"
"Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable licence to use a Deliverable."

elements.element: Paid-up licences are irrevocable (no at-will revocation, no expiry with Order Form term)
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable licence" replacing "revocable, non-transferable licence ... only during the applicable Order Form term"

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: Section 14.2/14.3 govern the Deliverable licence only; no subscription licence term is created or addressed here, so the condition is absent in the clause under review
"is transferable by Customer to a successor in accordance with Section 13.3"
"That licence extends to Customer's Affiliates" (covered without any notice condition)

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "transferable by Customer to a successor in accordance with Section 13.3"

reasons: The in-place replacement converts the revocable, term-limited Deliverable licence into a perpetual, irrevocable licence, and one concise added sentence supplies affiliates, contractors and successor transferability — all preferred elements are present.

The preferred subscription-termination element is conditionally absent: this clause grants only the paid-up Deliverable licence and does not create or govern subscription licence termination, so no language was required.

Minimality holds: the operative change is a targeted phrase replacement plus a single short sentence; Vendor's ownership of Deliverables, Vendor Technology retention, identification duty and third-party material restriction in 14.3 are untouched.

Only residual note (rationale, not a deviation): the added transfer right relies on a cross-reference to "Section 13.3"; confirm that section is the assignment/successor provision so the mechanic is not dangling.
